levelNote: Foundational questions on Georgian poets, war poetry, modern fiction and leading literary figures.

questions.question: Who edited the Georgian Poetry anthology series?
questions.explanation: Edward Marsh selected contemporary English verse for the five-volume anthology series.

questions.question: Which monarch gave the Georgian literary period its name?
questions.explanation: The Georgian poetic revival took its name from the reign of George V, beginning in 1910.

questions.question: How many volumes appeared in the original Georgian Poetry series?
questions.explanation: Five anthologies were issued over the years 1912 to 1922, creating a recognizable literary grouping.

questions.question: Which subject is particularly associated with much Georgian verse?
questions.explanation: Many Georgian poets preferred accessible language and familiar scenes of nature and ordinary life.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Georgian anthology movement:
I. The first Georgian Poetry anthology appeared in 1912.
II. Edward Marsh was its editor.
III. The anthology series consisted of a single volume.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The anthologies began in 1912 under Marsh and eventually ran to five volumes.

questions.question: Which poet wrote the war sonnet The Soldier?
questions.explanation: Brooke wrote The Soldier as part of his sequence of idealistic wartime sonnets.

questions.question: In which year did Rupert Brooke die?
questions.explanation: Brooke died in April 1915 before reaching the battlefields of Gallipoli.

questions.question: On which Greek island was Rupert Brooke buried?
questions.explanation: Brooke died while travelling with his naval unit and was buried on Skyros.

questions.question: Which quality best describes Brooke’s early war sonnets?
questions.explanation: His early war sonnets portray sacrifice in an idealistic, patriotic manner.

questions.question: Which location gives its name to one of Brooke’s nostalgic poems?
questions.explanation: The Old Vicarage, Grantchester recalls a Cambridgeshire village from afar.

questions.question: Which war poet wrote Dulce et Decorum Est?
questions.explanation: Owen attacks the supposed glory of war through images of exhausted soldiers and a gas attack.

questions.question: Which poet encouraged Wilfred Owen while both were at Craiglockhart?
questions.explanation: Owen met Sassoon at Craiglockhart in 1917 and benefited from his encouragement.

questions.question: Which poet wrote Break of Day in the Trenches?
questions.explanation: Rosenberg contrasts trench warfare with the ordinary movement of a rat at dawn.

questions.question: Which writer helped publish Wilfred Owen’s poems after his death?
questions.explanation: Sassoon supported Owen during the war and assisted the later publication of his work.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding First World War poetry:
I. Rupert Brooke often wrote in an idealistic patriotic tone.
II. Wilfred Owen frequently presented war as brutal and dehumanizing.
III. Siegfried Sassoon was a leading medieval epic poet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Brooke is associated with early patriotic ideals, while Owen and Sassoon exposed the costs of trench warfare.

questions.question: Which novel follows Paul Morel and his troubled family relationships?
questions.explanation: Sons and Lovers explores Paul Morel’s emotional entanglement with his mother and others.

questions.question: Which novel by D. H. Lawrence was suppressed in Britain in 1915?
questions.explanation: The Rainbow faced prosecution and suppression soon after publication in 1915.

questions.question: Which novel continues the story of the Brangwen sisters after The Rainbow?
questions.explanation: Women in Love follows characters and relationships developed from The Rainbow.

questions.question: What was the occupation of D. H. Lawrence’s father?
questions.explanation: Lawrence grew up in a Nottinghamshire mining family, a background visible in his fiction.

questions.question: Which late novel by Lawrence faced major obscenity controversy?
questions.explanation: Lady Chatterley’s Lover challenged sexual conventions and was long restricted in Britain.

questions.question: Which novel by Virginia Woolf follows preparations for a London party?
questions.explanation: Clarissa Dalloway plans a party while the narrative moves through memories and inner lives.

questions.question: What was the name of the press founded by Virginia and Leonard Woolf?
questions.explanation: The Woolfs founded the Hogarth Press in 1917 to print new literature.

questions.question: Which essay argues that a woman writer needs money and a room of her own?
questions.explanation: Woolf argues that material independence and space matter for women’s literary creation.

questions.question: Which London circle included Virginia Woolf and the critic Roger Fry?
questions.explanation: The Bloomsbury Group linked writers, artists and thinkers through friendship and discussion.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Virginia Woolf’s fiction:
I. Mrs Dalloway was published in 1925.
II. To the Lighthouse appeared in 1927.
III. Woolf wrote the novel Ulysses.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The first two novels are Woolf’s; Ulysses belongs to James Joyce.

questions.question: Which James Joyce book collects short stories about Dublin life?
questions.explanation: Dubliners presents ordinary lives in the Irish capital through fifteen short stories.

questions.question: On which date do the events of Ulysses take place?
questions.explanation: The action takes place during one day in Dublin, now commemorated as Bloomsday.

questions.question: Who is the central advertising canvasser in Joyce’s Ulysses?
questions.explanation: Leopold Bloom is one of the novel’s central figures, alongside Stephen Dedalus and Molly Bloom.

questions.question: Which term describes a sudden moment of insight in Joyce’s fiction?
questions.explanation: Joyce used epiphany for a revealing moment that changes the understanding of ordinary experience.

questions.question: Which novel traces Stephen Dedalus from schooldays toward leaving Ireland?
options: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man
questions.explanation: The novel traces Stephen Dedalus’s artistic and intellectual development before his departure from Ireland.

questions.question: Which modernist poem by T. S. Eliot appeared in 1922?
questions.explanation: The Waste Land portrays a fragmented modern civilization through multiple voices and allusions.

questions.question: Which Eliot poem presents an anxious speaker who hesitates over a social encounter?
options: The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock
questions.explanation: Prufrock’s anxious inner monologue presents a modern voice of hesitation.

questions.question: What is the opening section of The Waste Land called?
questions.explanation: The Burial of the Dead introduces the poem’s broken images of memory and renewal.

questions.question: How many sections make up The Waste Land?
questions.explanation: The poem consists of five separately titled sections.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding T. S. Eliot:
I. The Waste Land was published in 1922.
II. Eliot formulated the objective correlative in his criticism.
III. Eliot wrote A Room of One’s Own.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The first two claims concern Eliot; A Room of One’s Own was written by Virginia Woolf.

questions.question: Which Irish poet received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1923?
questions.explanation: Yeats was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1923 for his poetry and literary achievement.

questions.question: Which poem by Yeats imagines the collapse of an old historical order?
questions.explanation: The Second Coming imagines violent historical transformation through apocalyptic symbols.

questions.question: What does the phrase Celtic Twilight describe in Yeats’s early writing?
questions.explanation: Yeats’s early verse often draws on Irish legends, supernatural imagery and cultural revival.

questions.question: Which work sets out Yeats’s symbolic theory of historical cycles?
questions.explanation: A Vision explains a system of historical cycles and interlocking gyres.

questions.question: Which political event is the subject of Yeats’s poem Easter 1916?
questions.explanation: The poem considers the Irish uprising and the transformed lives of its participants.

questions.question: Who wrote the dystopian novel Brave New World?
questions.explanation: Huxley’s novel depicts a technologically managed future society.

questions.question: In which year was Brave New World first published?
questions.explanation: Brave New World appeared in 1932 as an early twentieth-century dystopia.

questions.question: What is soma in the society of Brave New World?
questions.explanation: Soma helps pacify citizens by providing chemical comfort instead of confronting distress.

questions.question: What genre best describes Brave New World?
questions.explanation: The novel imagines a frightening social order built around control, conditioning and pleasure.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the fictional World State:
I. People are conditioned from early life to fit social roles.
II. Consumer pleasure is used to discourage independent thought.
III. The society is governed by freely elected village councils.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The World State relies on conditioning and consumption, not democratic village government.

questions.question: Which poet is commonly associated with the Thirties Poets?
questions.explanation: Auden became a leading voice among the politically alert poets of the 1930s.

questions.question: What was the title of Auden’s influential 1930 collection?
questions.explanation: Poems, published in 1930, helped establish Auden’s reputation.

questions.question: Which historical conflict inspired Auden’s poem Spain?
questions.explanation: Auden wrote about the Spanish Civil War during the politically charged 1930s.

questions.question: Which poet belonged to the group often associated with Auden?
questions.explanation: Spender is regularly grouped with Auden, Day-Lewis and MacNeice among the 1930s poets.

questions.question: Which image source helped give some 1930s writers the nickname pylon poets?
questions.explanation: The nickname reflects their use of pylons, railways and machinery as poetic images.
